_doc: Point-in-time fact sheet for LLY retrospectives (retro/build_lly.py). Every value is tied to a source and becomes visible only on or after that source's 'published' date. A filing accepted after the 16:00 ET close is dated the next trading day ('filed' keeps the acceptance time, US Eastern; EDGAR gives only the filing date before 2003); the earnings 8-Ks of 2007-2009 were accepted before the open or during the session on their release days. The builder uses the latest history vintage published by AS_OF, the prints published by AS_OF that report a fiscal year after that history (a Q4 print reports the year just ended and extends the history until the 10-K), the guides for the current fiscal year (each field from the latest guide that states it) and the latest declared dividend (each vintage's, or a release's that first states a new rate: 'dividends'). Eli Lilly's fiscal year is the calendar year. EPS is GAAP diluted EPS from continuing operations before extraordinary items and accounting changes: the company's adjusted and pro forma figures also remove in-process research and development, which recurs, so they are shown and never used. 2008 is excluded (a loss). Guides: reported EPS ranges (the current-FY EPS; a range whose midpoint is a loss has no P/E) and the company's adjusted ranges (shown only); revenue growth is guided in words only, so BASE takes the latest quarter's sales growth excluding foreign exchange as each release states it. A print's growth and margins are derived from the raw figures of its release ('raw', $ millions; the builder re-derives and checks them), each against the year-ago quarter as the same release shows it. Company-wide U.S. and outside-U.S. growth is as each filing states it: in the release for Q4 2008 and 2009, in the 10-Q for Q2 2007 to Q3 2008 ('geo_later', visible from the 10-Q's date), in no filing for Q4 2007. Rule T's raw figures are in 'rule_t'. No later fact enters through this file: every source's published date bounds its use.

rule_t._doc: Rule T over fiscal 1997-2006, the decade of the FY2006 10-K (the vintage public on 2008-01-04): each annual change from the latest 10-K published by then that reports both years. U.S. net sales from the geographic data ('Net sales - to unaffiliated customers', United States), international being the consolidated total less the United States; the gross margin from the statements of income (net sales less cost of sales); net sales growth and the pre-tax margin (income from continuing operations before income taxes, extraordinary items and accounting changes, on net sales) from the five-year summaries. $ millions, as published: seams stay in (PCS discontinued from the FY1998 10-K; the geographic basis is the location of the selling subsidiary to the FY2003 10-K and of the customer from the FY2004 10-K, which restates 2002-2003; 2001's pre-tax income includes the debt-repurchase loss from the FY2003 10-K, SFAS 145).

price_basis: Yahoo's LLY series is adjusted for the 2-for-1 splits of 1995-12-21 and 1997-10-16; none follows 1997, and every P/E window here starts in 1998 or later, so Yahoo's close is the price as traded.
